memory_update.text: AMPH is the strongest underfollowed US-listed candidate for the regulated niche API supplier node found in this pass; verify third-party API revenue, DMF ownership, molecule-level concentration, and FDA inspection history.
RDY provides direct India API/DMF/USFDA-inspected exposure and may fit China-plus-one API diversification, but it is broader and more visible than a narrow niche molecule supplier.
TEVA/TAPI and Lonza should be retained as reference anchors for API/CDMO scale, regulated manufacturing expectations, and market-pricing comparison rather than primary underfollowed alpha candidates.

Many pure-play niche API manufacturers are India- or Europe-listed rather than US exchange-listed; future passes should decide whether US OTC ADRs and foreign ordinary tickers are allowed for a fuller small/mid-cap discovery lane.

node: Regulated niche API suppliers with customer re-validation lock-in
summary: Expanded the universe around regulated API suppliers where DMF filings, cGMP/FDA-inspected sites, customer qualification, and molecule-specific process know-how may create switching friction. The cleanest US-listed underfollowed candidate found in this pass is Amphastar, because it explicitly sells API products, owns API manufacturing assets, and focuses on technically challenging injectables. Dr. Reddy's is a more visible Indian API/formulations ADR with broad DMF depth. Teva/TAPI and Lonza are reference anchors rather than underfollowed small/mid-cap ideas; they help map the competitive/regulatory context for API CDMO and drug-substance supply.
